title: Distance from a Point on a Line to the Origin as a Function of x
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Consider a point (x, y) lying on the line 2x + 4y = 5. Let L be the Euclidean distance from the point (x, y) to the origin (0, 0). Express L as a function of x.

steps.title: Write the Distance Formula from (x, y) to the Origin
steps.explanation: By the Euclidean distance formula in the plane, the distance L from (x, y) to (0, 0) is sqrt(x^2 + y^2).
steps.why: The distance between (x, y) and (0, 0) is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs |x| and |y|.

steps.title: Solve the Line Equation for y in Terms of x
steps.explanation: Isolate y in the linear constraint 2x + 4y = 5 so that y can be eliminated from the distance formula.
steps.why: Every point (x, y) on the line must satisfy y = (5 - 2x)/4.

steps.title: Substitute y and Simplify Under a Common Denominator
steps.explanation: Substitute y = (5 - 2x)/4 into L = sqrt(x^2 + y^2), expand (5 - 2x)^2 = 25 - 20x + 4x^2, combine over the common denominator 16, and take sqrt(16) = 4 out of the denominator.
steps.why: Combining fractions under the radical allows factoring 1/sqrt(16) = 1/4 out of the square root.
